| --- | --- | --- |

Use the first rung that works:

3. A clippy or rustc lint already in the workspace lints.

# Agent guide

Rules for AI agents working in this repo.

## Crates

| Crate | License | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| callisto-model | MIT | none (external: `michi-graph`, MIT) |
| callisto-manifests | FSL-1.1-MIT | model |
| callisto-graph | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests |
| callisto-cli | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests, graph |
| callisto-fixtures | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) |

- `callisto-model` (MIT) must never depend on an FSL crate. It depends on `michi-graph` (MIT, no dependencies of its own) for dependency-graph validation and ordering. `just license-boundary` fails if anything it builds with is FSL.
- Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml` after adding or moving a crate.

## Commands

- Full pipeline: `just ci` (includes the 90% coverage gate). `just test`, `just lint`, `just fmt`.
- Before every push or PR: `just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test`, and `just ci` before marking a PR ready. Judge each by its exit code. Never tail or grep the output for success (a compile error prints no "failed" line), and never report a check as passed that was not run.
- Commits must be signed: the ruleset requires it. Never pass `-c commit.gpgsign=false`. After pushing, `gh api repos/orin-dx/callisto/commits/<sha> --jq .commit.verification.reason` must say `valid`.
- Performance: `just bench` times `status`, `version --dry-run` and `release --dry-run` over generated workspaces and counts the git processes each starts (`CALLISTO_BENCH_SHAPES=1` lists which). A change that adds a git process per package fails review.
- Scoped iteration: one `cargo test -p <crate>` or `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` at a time.
  - Not `moon run <project>:test`: its per-project fan-out serializes on `target/`'s build lock.
  - Never run cargo builds in parallel.
- Changesets: `callisto add --package cargo/callisto-cli:<bump> --summary "..."` (non-interactive). Target `callisto-cli`: its changelog is the one users read. One changeset per user-visible topic. Lead with what the user sees now and say why it matters to them; add an action or limit when it matters. A fix to something not yet released has no changeset. Use a short sentence for a simple change, or a short lead and bullets for related details. No internal names, mechanism or filler.
- Never `git checkout -- Cargo.lock` as cleanup. A lockfile diff means investigate, not discard.

## Invariants

1. Safe Rust only: `unsafe_code = "forbid"`.
2. Manifest edits preserve format: `toml_edit` for TOML; JSON changes that only replace string values are written into the original text by span (`json_text`), anything else keeps key order and fingerprinted indentation. No regex or line edits.
3. File writes go through `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write`.
4. User-facing errors derive `miette::Diagnostic` with a code and a fix.
5. No emojis in docs or code.
6. No cargo features in shipped crates; behaviour is chosen at runtime (#143). The dev-only `callisto-model/test-util` feature is the exception.
7. No `unwrap()` outside tests (`just lint` denies it). An `expect` names the invariant that makes it unreachable.

## Enforcing an invariant

Use the first rung that works:

1. A type, or a private constructor or field, so the wrong thing cannot compile.
2. An exhaustive `match` with no `_` arm on our own enums.
3. A clippy or rustc lint already in the workspace lints.
4. One small test that drives the real binary or function and checks observable behavior.

CI runs it | | `just zizmor` | Static security audit of workflow/action YAML (requires `zizmor`) | | `just workflow-contracts` | Release-workflow contract/policy tests, action pin verification, installer tests — what the CI `workflow-contracts` job runs besides actionlint | | `just release-workflow-behavior` | Release lifecycle exercised at the real CLI boundary with faked registry/Git/forge/attestation providers | | `just pre-commit` | `fmt-check` only — fast, runs on every local commit via the installed hook | | `just pre-push` | `fmt-check` + `lint-affected` — runs on every local push via the installed hook | | `just hooks` | Installs the native `pre-commit`/`pre-push` git hooks above | | `just clean` | Clears moon task caches, `cargo clean`, removes `lcov.info` / `callisto-schema.json` | Maintainer-only recipes not part of the normal PR loop: `mutants` (mutation testing), `fuzz` (runs a fuzz target; # caliper-docgen

Faster than react-docgen-typescript; measured numbers are in `docs/performance.md`. OXC parses TypeScript/TSX; we extract React component props and emit RDT-compatible JSON via `--format rdt`. See `docs/STATUS.md` for current state and known gaps.

## Commands

```bash
just lint doc-check machete typos          # what CI runs; pass before pushing
cargo test -p caliper-docgen-core          # unit + snapshot tests
cargo clippy -p caliper-docgen-core -- -D warnings
cargo build --release                         # full build including CLI
```

Or use `/check` and `/snapshot` for the common workflows.

## Non-negotiables

1. No `unwrap()` outside `#[cfg(test)]` — use `?`
2. `FxHashMap` for internal maps; `BTreeMap` for JSON-output maps
3. `CompactString` for type/prop names in hot paths
4. No AST refs escape `parse_file()` — allocator is local per call
5. No terminal/display code in `crates/core`
6. Always emit `Diagnostic` when degrading — never fail silently

## Architecture

```
OXC parse → SourceData (extractor/) → GlobalSourceData (pipeline/) → ComponentEntry (resolver/) → ExtractionOutput
```

No reverse dependencies. `pub(crate)` for implementation modules; `pub` only for consumer-facing API (`pipeline/`, `types/`, `react_types`).

See `ARCHITECTURE.md` for the full pipeline/crate-graph overview, and `docs/architecture/` for per-subsystem invariants and known gaps (pipeline orchestration, extractor, resolver, types, serialization, CLI, NAPI binding) — start at `docs/architecture/README.md`.

## Decisions

Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing the parser choice, `PropType` serialization, the DTS cache format, panic containment or the semantic backend. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR.

## Testing discipline

Two habits that repeatedly caught real bugs during the 2026-08-12 spec-validation pass (a stale-by-one-edit watch mode, always-zero watch stats — both had zero test coverage despite extensive existing suites):

1. **Sibling-path parity.** When a function parallels an already-tested one (e.g. `WatchSession::update_file` mirrors `extract()`'s resolve/panic-containment logic; `create_session`'s guard boundary mirrors `initialize_session`/`extract_file_incremental`'s), the new path needs a test asserting the _same_ contract, not just "it runs without error." A sibling path is exactly where coverage silently lapses.
2. **Assert content, not presence.** Prefer `assert_eq!` against an exact expected value over `contains(...)`/`is_some()`/liveness checks wherever the cost is comparable. A test asserting "component X exists" survives X's props resolving to stale or wrong data; a test asserting X's exact prop set does not.

## Crate guide

- `crates/core` — pure extraction logic; @crates/core/AGENTS.md
- `crates/cli` — clap CLI, no logic; @crates/cli/AGENTS.md
- `crates/binding` — thin NAPI wrapper, delegates to core
- `crates/semantic` — TypeScript 7.1 checker backend, on by default (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`)

## Scripts

No new sh, py or mjs script unless a CI job, the weekly or a documented recipe calls it; prefer a Rust test or the existing oracle TypeScript. A measurement run once is recorded in docs (`docs/measurement.md`, `docs/gate-measurements.md`), not committed as a script. Each script's caller is listed in `docs/measurement.md`.

## Plugins

Start work through these commands so their checks run:

- Options before deciding: `/guide:explore`. Does it work: `/guide:spike`.
- Bug or review findings: `/guide:fix`. Real feature or shared change: `/guide:build`.
- Verify or find bugs: `/guide:check`. Commit message: `/guide:ship`.

Pull requests are opened by Entire from the branch's trail, so `/guide:ship` stops at the commit.

## Writing and commits

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler. Banned words are in `docs/adr/README.md`.
- Changesets become bullets under generated changelog headings. Write one short, consumer-facing paragraph per changeset; start with the outcome, and include an upgrade action or cost when needed. Do not start the body with a heading or list marker.
- Never hard-wrap Markdown, commit messages or PR descriptions: one line per paragraph.
- Comments: only the non-obvious why, no history (the commit records it). Fill to 120 columns (`.rustfmt.toml`). Rewriting a comment block counts as writing it: re-fill and cut it, don't inherit the old wrapping.
- Commits: imperative subject, at most one or two sentences of why, no list of what changed, no "This commit...". Skip the body when the subject says it all.

Say what you expected, what happened, and, if it's a spec-vs-reality mismatch, which file in `docs/spec/` you were reading.
